codeReview.decision: No new confirmed P0/P1 in the subsequent trusted-clock patch.
observations: calendarDraftCapability derives the reference calendar date in the host-provided IANA zone, then increments a UTC representation of that calendar date. This computes the next local date across month/year/DST boundaries without assuming every local day is 24 elapsed hours.

Both chat entry points append the same host-clock instructions to the effective system prompt. Without an admitted calendar context, no instructions or calendar tool are added. The backend constructor validates the timezone and supplies referenceTime.toISOString(), rather than lifting arbitrary conversation text into this instruction.

The tool remains draft-only, with unchanged exact user excerpt check, offset/timezone match, interval validation, once-per-Run staging, sourceRequestID, needs_review and external_effect=none. Human confirmation is still required.

This is a prompt-authority clarification; semantic relative-date correctness remains model-dependent and is not newly enforced by deterministic tool validation. A fresh real batch is still needed to demonstrate improvement.
